sections.h2: Three ways to sell a Lancaster house
sections.html:
Homeowners here choose between an agent, a self-found buyer and a cash purchase. Timing and the building's condition drive the choice. If you have a neat ranch and no deadline, listing makes sense. If the roof is failing, a probate is pending or a tenant is refusing to leave, a fast as-is buyer is the likelier fit.

  • Agent listing: the most visibility, along with showings, an appraisal for the buyer's lender and some risk that financing collapses.
  • Owner-handled sale: you decide price and terms while your attorney writes the contract and deed.
  • Cash purchase: the buyer accepts the property as it stands, so there are no repair requests and no mortgage contingency.

Whichever you pick, the sale ends with a notarized deed, transfer tax forms filed with the Erie County Clerk, and any back tax on the parcel paid off.

Lancaster sits in Erie County, roughly 11 miles east of downtown Buffalo, on about 37 square miles. Two villages lie inside it, Lancaster and Depew. Population is 45,075, close to the 45,106 counted in 2020.

Five school districts bill Lancaster addresses: Lancaster Central, Depew Union Free, Alden Central, Clarence Central and Iroquois Central. Lancaster Central covers most of the town, though buyers should hear the district named on your own tax bill. Driving is simple: the Thruway (I-90) runs across the north end, US 20 follows Broadway through the center, and NY 78 (Transit Road) marks the western side.

Owners near Broadway in the village should ask the village what historic review applies before promising a buyer a facade or window project. The Building Department's page carries a Village of Lancaster historic preservation application.

Owner-occupants hold about four in five homes, and the middle one is worth $277,600. No midpoint prices a specific house, so pull recent sales from your own area before picking a figure.

Gross rent is $1,079 at the midpoint and household income $89,080. The town counts 19,722 households, and 22.1% of its residents are 65 or older. A 20-minute average commute is one of the quieter selling points for a house here.

Earlier renovations sometimes surface during a sale. The Building Department enforces the state building and fire code, zoning, stormwater practices and flood plain rules across both the town and the village, and nobody may build, alter, move or demolish a structure without a permit.

The office posts applications for decks, fences, pools and hot tubs, sheds, signs, demolition and one- and two-family dwellings, along with a handout on as-built survey requirements. If a deck, an addition or a finished basement went in before you bought, ask whether the project is on file and was signed off. A clear answer saves negotiating time later.

  • Inspections tied to a permit are booked by phone with the office, which keeps weekday hours.
  • The department also links resources on vacant and "zombie" properties, handy for an inherited house that has sat empty.
  • Truck routes and yard sale permits are separate matters handled through the town and its Highway Department.

Before listing, ask the office for the permit file on your address and read it once. Knowing what is recorded lets you answer a buyer's attorney the same day.

Pay Town and County tax by February 15 and school tax by October 15. A weekend or holiday pushes either date to the next day. The tax office inside the Town Clerk's office collects both. For mailed checks the postmark must show the due date or earlier. The office allows no exceptions.

Lancaster late-payment rules
BillLate penaltyWhere unpaid tax goes
School (due October 15)7.5% for the rest of October, 9% through NovemberErie County tax roll after November 30
Town and County (due February 15)1.5% in the first two weeks, rising to 7.5% by end of April, then interestErie County after June 30

The town office takes Town and County payments through June 30 and school payments through November 30. Past those dates, payments and payoff questions go to Erie County Real Property Tax Services in Buffalo. Because interest changes the payoff monthly, get the county's number before choosing a closing date.

If you cannot pay before the school deadline, the unpaid amount moves to the county after November 30 and costs more every month. Selling a house with that balance is workable: the payoff comes out of your proceeds at closing, and the buyer's attorney will want the county's written figure.

sections.h2: Erie County deed charges and transfer tax
sections.html:
Sellers here pay two layers of transfer tax, the state's $2.00 and the county's $2.50, which makes $4.50 per $500 of price. The Clerk rounds the price up to the next $500.

Recording costs a $45 statutory fee plus $5 a page. Filing the TP-584 is $10, and the RP-5217 report is $125 for residential property. The deed must carry original signatures, a notary's acknowledgment, a full legal description and street addresses for every party, since P.O. boxes are rejected.

  • Owners 62 or older who have lived a year or more in a one- or two-family house may qualify for a reduced $2.00-per-$500 rate.
  • Buyers of residential property at $1 million or above owe an extra 1% mansion tax.
  • The Clerk also asks for a Notice of Sale or Transfer of Ownership on residential property.

File the TP-584 and pay within 15 days of delivering the deed. After closing, end your STAR registration so the next owner can sign up for the credit.

sections.h2: Sorting out a damaged or inherited house
sections.html:
Storm or fire damage does not stop a sale. Offer the house as-is to investors, list it at a repair-adjusted price, or accept cash from a buyer who skips the repair list. Ask the Building Department about open permits first.

Cash buyers do not need an appraisal or a loan approval, so nothing there delays you. The sequence runs from a written offer to a title search, then signing the deed and transfer forms, then payment on closing day. Bring your latest tax bills, permit paperwork and, for an estate, whatever proves who is authorized to sign. Get payoff figures from the tax office and the county, and your closing attorney can settle any unpaid tax from the proceeds. That payoff step is easy to forget and can hold up the closing if the figure arrives late.

faqs.q: Which office collects tax on a Lancaster property?
faqs.a: Pay at the tax office in the Town Clerk's office for Town, County and school bills. After June 30 (Town and County) or November 30 (school), the payment goes to Erie County Real Property Tax Services in Buffalo.

faqs.q: Does Lancaster belong to one school district?
faqs.a: No. Lancaster Central covers most of it, yet Depew Union Free, Alden Central, Clarence Central and Iroquois Central also bill Lancaster addresses. Read your own tax bill to see which one applies.

faqs.q: Who covers transfer tax on a Lancaster sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays both the state and Erie County portions when the deed goes to the County Clerk, $4.50 per $500 in all. Owners 62 and older who qualify may pay a reduced $2.00 rate.

faqs.q: Must I get a permit before listing my Lancaster house?
faqs.a: A plain sale is not among the permit triggers. The rule covers building, altering, moving and demolishing, so call the Building Department to confirm that earlier decks, pools or additions were permitted and closed out.

faqs.q: Is a damaged Lancaster house still sellable?
faqs.a: Yes. Sell it as-is, list it with the repairs priced in, or take cash from a buyer who wants no repair list. Check open permits with the Building Department before saying yes to any offer.
